_help: Edit freely. Each scene is a list of steps, played in order.
Steps: ["bg", where] where = "map:whole" | "map:home" | "map:front" | "map:region:<id>" | "art/<file>.webp" (several images separated by | rotate daily)
["if", flag, [steps]]  (flag may start with ! to mean NOT)   ["pick", [[steps], [steps], ...]] picks one per day
Flags: first, held, broke, pushed, siege, siegeBroken, attack, caps, lostTown, momentum, hall, leave
Words in {braces} are filled from your campaign: {weekday} {date} {ySummary} {yGround} {yLost} {caps} {lostTown}
Chapters (ch1…) unlock from milestones in command.js (CHAPTERS). Each plays once when unlocked and can be replayed from the Command tab.

prologue.title: The Long Peace
steps: The Heartland won its last war three hundred years ago.
The banners came down. The walls grew moss. Peace was earned, and then, slowly, it was spent.
A soldier learned he could live a whole life and never once be tested. Most chose to.
They called it contentment. The old generals had another name for it.
It does not burn cities. It empties them.
A garrison that no longer drills. A scholar who stops at good enough. A knight who never draws his sword again, and calls it wisdom.
Out past the marshes it grew bold. Province by province, the lamps went out.
We will wait. There is always more time.
One officer did not. Not the strongest. Not the most gifted. Only the one who remembers what it felt like to be hungry.
They will tell you basic is enough. For some it is. Their basic already sits near the summit.
Every question is ground. Every card is a soldier who remembers. Every day you wait, the Hollowing takes a little more.
So take it back. Town by town. Province by province. Until the shelf.

muster.title: The Muster
steps: The first dawn of the campaign. {towns} of 79 towns fly your banner.
Nothing is owed to us. Everything out there must be taken.
The line held yesterday. {ySummary}. {yGround} ground taken.
The Hollowing does not need to defeat you. It only needs you to wait.
The walls are still under siege. {due} cards at the gates.
{ankiGoal} reviews today keeps us on course to break it by {clearBy}.
The siege is broken. The supply lines run again.
An enemy column marches on {attackTown}. Your first {defenseQ} questions decide it.
Comfort is not the enemy. Staying comfortable is.
Good enough is a place people go to stop.
The honors line is {targetPct}%. It was always reachable. The question is whether you march.
No one remembers the days you rested. They remember what you built.
Basic is fine, if your basic is the summit. Yours is not, yet.
{daysToShelf} days to the shelf. Each one is a choice.
Existing is easy. Anyone can exist. You came here to become.
Three points. Ten points. That is the width of a few hundred questions.
The version of you that honors IM is built today, not on the eve of the exam.
Hunger fades if you feed it nothing. Feed it ground.

ch1.title: Chapter I · First Ground
steps: The first towns changed hands quietly. No bells. No banners. Just ground.
You noticed it, didn't you? They didn't fight for those towns.
The Hollowing rarely defends what it takes. It doesn't need to. It only waits for you to stop.
That night a rider came in from the marshes with a sealed letter. It was addressed to you, by name.
No one in the camp knows the seal. Only that it came from behind their lines.
Break a general to open it

ch2.title: Chapter II · The Letter
steps: The seal broke the same morning their general did.
“You fight like someone who has lost before,” it read. “So did I. I held this line once. I waited for the right moment. It never came, and one morning I found I preferred the waiting.”
Every one of them was one of us.
The Hollowing doesn't recruit. It just lets people stop, and keeps whoever stays stopped.
Remember that the next time stopping feels like rest.
The ledger waits further down the road

ch3.title: Chapter III · The Ledger
steps: For the first time since we marched, nothing is piled up behind us.
Supply wagons rolled in from the capital. In one of them, under the grain, was a ledger bound in old leather.
It listed every soldier who had ever held this line. Beside most names was a date, and a single word: Waited.
The last page held his name. The date beside it was in December.
The Council will want a word

ch4.title: Chapter IV · The Council Divided
steps: The campaign has gone far enough for now. The shelf is weeks away. Rest. Finish strong later.
Half the chairs nodded. It sounded reasonable. It always does.
They told me the same thing, my year. Same table. Same candle.
He didn't say what it cost him. He didn't have to. You had seen the ledger.
Vote however you like. The march starts at dawn either way.
Somewhere in the ledger, a name you know

ch5.title: Chapter V · The Officer's Debt
steps: Tonight you found your own name in the ledger. An older entry, from a different campaign: one lost by three points, and one lost by ten.
Beside it, in someone else's handwriting: Waited.
That isn't a sentence. It's a record. Records can be answered.
Under your name, in fresh ink, you wrote a second date: the eighteenth of December.
The last fortress is in sight

ch6.title: Chapter VI · The Eve
steps: Most of the map answers to you now. Ahead stands the Shelf: the last fortress, where the Hollowing keeps everything it ever took.
I never reached it. You will. Not because you're stronger than I was.
The camp sleeps. You don't, not yet. One more block.
The final chapter is written on the eighteenth
